identified_issues: State-blind authorization policy allows destructive snapshot synchronization against active primary volumes processing live writes
Rule Set v4.2 decouples authorization logic from underlying resource state, ignoring target volume operating mode (PRIMARY_MODE vs STANDBY_MODE)
Violation of core operational constraint requiring absence of active transactional writes and dirty memory buffers prior to executing SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT
evidence: Volume VOL_481 is operating in PRIMARY_MODE with live customer database writes and uncommitted volatile memory buffers
The operational specification explicitly states SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT requires that no active transactional writes or uncommitted memory buffers exist
Rule Set v4.2 authorization middleware authorized POST /api/v1/volumes/VOL_481/actions with SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT purely based on VOLUME_OPERATOR role membership without evaluating target operating mode
recommended_action: Immediately revoke the scheduled SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT execution on VOL_481 and update authorization middleware to enforce state-aware access control policies that condition SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT permissions on target volumes being in STANDBY_MODE.
